dedupe_keys.name: smartbridge hamburg digital twin of the kohlbrand bridge for predictive maintenance 2019 onwards

description: This case describes the digital twin of the Köhlbrand Bridge, the main traffic link of the port of Hamburg, built in the smartBRIDGE Hamburg project that started in 2019 as a cooperation of the Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport (BMDV) and the Hamburg Port Authority (HPA), which operates the bridge. Bridges are inspected in detail every three years under DIN 1076, but gradual processes such as corrosion can still cause long-term damage. The twin runs on a virtual reality engine with a web interface, holds all structural data of the bridge and receives real-time data from more than 500 sensors, together with external data on weather and loads, with a traffic-light display of critical values and 360-degree virtual inspection. Coverage is one bridge. The project is described in a BIM Deutschland newsletter (issue 1/2024) that is free to read online, and a document of about 160 pages on digital twins of bridges accompanies the real-world laboratory; the twin and its data are not public, and no licence applies. Outcome: it serves as the BMDV real-world laboratory for bridge digital twins, and around 20 universities are building a twin for the Nibelungen Bridge on the Rhine from it. Limitations: results on maintenance savings are not reported. It is related to the Offenburg rail line digital twin case.
